stem:
The mean mass of packets of sugar is supposed to be 505 g. A random sample of 10 packets filled by a certain machine was taken and the masses, in grams, were found to be as follows.

$$500 \qquad 499 \qquad 496 \qquad 495 \qquad 498 \qquad 490 \qquad 492 \qquad 501 \qquad 494 \qquad 494$$

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: The mean mass of packets produced by this machine was found to be less than 505 g, so the machine was adjusted. Following the adjustment, the masses of a random sample of 150 packets from the machine were measured and the total mass was found to be $75\,660$ g.
parts.text: Given that the population standard deviation is 3.6 g, test at the 2% significance level whether the machine is still producing packets with mean mass less than 505 g.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Explain why the use of the normal distribution is justified in carrying out the test in part **(ii)**.
